How to Plan a Kitchen Remodel in Tampa

By Unique Building Contractors · October 15, 2026

The short answer

Start a Tampa kitchen remodel by identifying what does not work in the room, deciding whether the layout will change, and documenting appliances and cabinetry before requesting a detailed proposal.

Begin with the way you use the kitchen

List the problems you want to solve before collecting finish samples. A crowded cooking aisle, a dishwasher that blocks a cabinet, or a shortage of landing space requires a different response from worn surfaces. Walk through breakfast, grocery unloading, and a family dinner to see where movement becomes difficult.

For example, replacing cabinets in their existing positions may improve storage without solving a narrow passage. Moving an island could help circulation, but it can also affect flooring, outlets, lighting, and the ceiling above. Ask for those consequences to be considered together.

Coordinate appliances, cabinetry and surfaces

Choose appliance dimensions early enough for cabinet planning. Record refrigerator clearances, range requirements, hood locations, and how doors will open. Cabinet drawings should show fillers, panels, organizers, and the location of switches or outlets that might otherwise be concealed.

A useful selection sheet identifies the cabinet finish, hardware, sink, faucet, countertop, backsplash, and lighting. Distinguish a confirmed selection from an allowance so that a proposal does not appear more complete than it is. Keep alternate choices available for items with uncertain lead times.

Create a practical construction plan

Before work begins, agree on protection for adjacent rooms, access for deliveries, storage for appliances, and a temporary food preparation area. Clarify who removes packaging and debris and when the kitchen will be unavailable.

Your written scope should explain demolition, trade work, installation, finishing, and cleanup. Ask how site discoveries and requested changes will be documented. A clear decision process is more useful than a schedule that assumes every selection and existing condition is already resolved.

Your planning checklist

  • Write down three functional problems.
  • Confirm appliance sizes before cabinet approval.
  • Separate selected products from allowances.
  • Agree on a temporary kitchen and delivery access.

Common questions

Should I keep my current kitchen layout?

Keep it if it supports the way you cook and move through the room. Compare the functional benefit of a new layout with the additional work it creates before deciding.
